package mapper

// This file is copied into a generated project by
// v1.assertJSONColumnDriverValue and run there with `go test ./entity/mapper/`.
// It needs no module substitution: it is in the mapper package itself and imports
// only the standard library.

import (
	"bytes"
	"database/sql"
	"database/sql/driver"
	"encoding/json"
	"io"
	"testing"
)

// recordingDriver is a database/sql driver that records the argument values it is
// handed and does nothing else.
//
// It deliberately does NOT implement driver.NamedValueChecker, so arguments reach
// it through driver.DefaultParameterConverter — the same Valuer hop
// go-sql-driver/mysql's own converter takes. What lands in args is therefore what
// the real driver would render into the SQL text under interpolateParams=true.
type recordingDriver struct{ args []driver.Value }

func (d *recordingDriver) Open(string) (driver.Conn, error) { return &recordingConn{d: d}, nil }

type recordingConn struct{ d *recordingDriver }

func (c *recordingConn) Prepare(string) (driver.Stmt, error) { return &recordingStmt{d: c.d}, nil }
func (c *recordingConn) Close() error                        { return nil }
func (c *recordingConn) Begin() (driver.Tx, error)           { return nil, io.EOF }

type recordingStmt struct{ d *recordingDriver }

func (s *recordingStmt) Close() error  { return nil }
func (s *recordingStmt) NumInput() int { return 1 }
func (s *recordingStmt) Exec(args []driver.Value) (driver.Result, error) {
	s.d.args = append(s.d.args, args...)
	return driver.RowsAffected(0), nil
}
func (s *recordingStmt) Query([]driver.Value) (driver.Rows, error) { return nil, io.EOF }

// TestJSONColumnReachesDriverAsString is the regression test for the bug that made
// every write to a JSON column fail on a MySQL DSN with interpolateParams=true:
//
//	Error 3144 (22032): Cannot create a JSON value from a string with CHARACTER
//	SET 'binary'
//
// With that flag the driver renders the SQL text itself, and its []byte branch
// emits a BINARY string literal (_binary'{"a":1}') that MySQL will not cast to
// JSON. The type of the value the driver receives is the whole bug: a
// json.RawMessage assigned into a []byte params field is erased back to []byte
// long before the driver sees it, so no amount of wrapping at the call site helps.
// The column type has to hand the driver a string, which is what JSON.Value does.
func TestJSONColumnReachesDriverAsString(t *testing.T) {
	d := &recordingDriver{}
	sql.Register("jsoncolumnprobe", d)
	db, err := sql.Open("jsoncolumnprobe", "")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("open: %v", err)
	}
	defer db.Close()

	if _, err := db.Exec("INSERT INTO t (c) VALUES (?)", JSON(`{"a":1}`)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("exec: %v", err)
	}
	if len(d.args) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("expected one argument, got %d", len(d.args))
	}

	got, ok := d.args[0].(string)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("the driver received %T; go-sql-driver/mysql renders a []byte argument as "+
			"_binary'...' under interpolateParams=true, which MySQL rejects for a JSON column "+
			"(Error 3144). A JSON column parameter must reach the driver as a string.", d.args[0])
	}
	if got != `{"a":1}` {
		t.Errorf("driver received %q, want the JSON document verbatim", got)
	}
}

// An empty value must be SQL NULL, not the empty string: no JSON column accepts
// '' (MySQL error 3140, "Invalid JSON text: The document is empty"). This is what
// mapper.NullifyEmptyJSON used to do at each call site, and it now covers required
// columns too, which that call site never did.
func TestJSONColumnEmptyIsNull(t *testing.T) {
	for _, empty := range []JSON{nil, {}} {
		v, err := empty.Value()
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("Value: %v", err)
		}
		if v != nil {
			t.Errorf("empty JSON produced %#v, want nil (SQL NULL)", v)
		}
	}
}

// Reading back a NULL JSON column is why the column type is not plain
// json.RawMessage: database/sql cannot scan NULL into a bare named slice type
// ("unsupported Scan, storing driver.Value type <nil> into type *json.RawMessage").
func TestJSONColumnScan(t *testing.T) {
	var j JSON
	if err := j.Scan(nil); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("scanning NULL: %v", err)
	}
	if j != nil {
		t.Errorf("NULL scanned to %q, want nil", j)
	}

	if err := j.Scan(`{"a":1}`); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("scanning string: %v", err)
	}
	if string(j) != `{"a":1}` {
		t.Errorf("scanned %q, want the document verbatim", j)
	}

	// The copy is load-bearing: the generated list layer scans straight into the
	// repository model's fields, and the []byte a driver hands to Scan is only
	// valid until the next call. Retaining it would alias one row's buffer into
	// every row of the response.
	src := []byte(`{"a":1}`)
	if err := j.Scan(src); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("scanning bytes: %v", err)
	}
	copy(src, []byte(`{"b":2}`))
	if string(j) != `{"a":1}` {
		t.Errorf("Scan retained the driver's buffer: value changed to %q when the source was reused", j)
	}

	if err := j.Scan(42); err == nil {
		t.Error("scanning an int into a JSON column should fail")
	}
}

// A repository model carries json tags (sqlc's emit_json_tags), so the column has
// to marshal as its contents rather than as a base64 byte slice.
func TestJSONColumnMarshalsVerbatim(t *testing.T) {
	out, err := json.Marshal(struct {
		Payload JSON `json:"payload"`
	}{Payload: JSON(`{"a":1}`)})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("marshal: %v", err)
	}
	if !bytes.Contains(out, []byte(`"payload":{"a":1}`)) {
		t.Errorf("marshaled to %s, want the JSON document embedded verbatim", out)
	}
}
